title: H3598 (126th General Assembly): Reporting information to SLED, firearms background checks

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Draft, 2025-02-05; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/prever/3598_20250205.htm (LegiScan doc 3103881))
provenance.note: Version read is the "Draft" print dated 2025-02-05 (not an enrolled act); version_read "other". No passage vote on record. Sections 1-3 (clerk, magistrate, municipal judge reports) also add domestic-violence, stalking and bond orders to the 48-hour list; counted as part of the same gun-prohibition reporting scheme.

operative_text:
Section 5 (new Section 16-23-920, Article 9): For any sale or transfer of a firearm for which a licensed dealer contacts the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) to conduct a background check, a licensed gun dealer may not deliver a firearm to any transferee unless the NICS provides the licensed dealer with a unique identification number or five days have elapsed from the date the licensed dealer contacted the NICS and the NICS has not notified the licensed dealer that a sale or transfer to such person would violate state or federal law.
Section 5 (new Section 16-23-930): A person who violates the provisions of this article is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, must be imprisoned not more than three years or fined not more than one thousand dollars, or both.
Section 4 (new Section 23-1-260): Each law enforcement agency must report to the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) within twenty-four hours: ... (3) any incident in which a person may be prohibited from obtaining or possessing a firearm by state or federal law.
Section 1 (Section 14-17-325): Every clerk of court shall also report to the State Law Enforcement Division, within forty-eight hours, the issuance, rescission, or termination of any: ... (6) orders of state firearms prohibition pursuant to Section 16-25-30; and (7) other restraining orders, orders of protection, or other orders that prohibit a person from legally purchasing or possessing a firearm, but only upon being directed to transmit such orders by the appropriate judge.
